q: What is this animal?
f: No two zebras have exactly the same stripe pattern.

q: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
f: Its red colour comes from iron oxide, or rust, in the soil.

q: Which city is famous for these canals?
f: Amsterdam has more than 160 canals.

q: What is the largest animal on Earth?
f: It can grow to about 30 metres long.

q: How many legs does a spider have?
f: Insects have six legs, so spiders are not insects.

q: At what temperature does water boil at sea level?
f: That's 212 degrees Fahrenheit.

q: Which instrument is this?
f: A violin usually has four strings.

q: What is the tallest animal in the world?
f: A giraffe's neck has seven bones, the same as a human's.

q: Which fruit is this?
f: A pineapple takes about two years to grow.

q: Which bird is this?
f: Flamingos get their pink colour from the food they eat.

q: What is the highest mountain on Earth?
f: Its summit is about 8,849 metres above sea level.

q: What is the capital of Turkey?
f: Ankara became the capital of Turkey in 1923.

q: Which gas makes up most of Earth's air?
f: Nitrogen makes up about 78 percent of the air.

q: In which country is this temple?
f: Borobudur is the largest Buddhist temple in the world.

q: Which mammal lays eggs?
f: Platypuses and echidnas are the only mammals that lay eggs.

q: How many strings does a standard guitar have?
f: Bass guitars usually have four.

q: What is the largest country in the world by area?
f: Russia spans eleven time zones.

q: Which metal is liquid at room temperature?
f: Mercury was once used in most thermometers.

q: What is the longest river in South America?
f: The Amazon carries more water than any other river.

q: How many teeth does an adult usually have?
f: That includes the four wisdom teeth.

q: In which country is this waterfall?
f: Angel Falls is the highest uninterrupted waterfall in the world.

q: What is the capital of Brazil?
f: Brasília was built from scratch and opened in 1960.

q: Which bird can fly backwards?
f: Some hummingbirds beat their wings more than 50 times a second.

q: What is the chemical symbol for sodium?
f: Na comes from natrium, its Latin name.

q: In which country is this ancient monument?
f: Stonehenge was built around 5,000 years ago.

q: How many hearts does an octopus have?
f: Its blood is blue because it is rich in copper.

q: Which country is home to this bird, the kiwi?
f: The kiwi is a flightless bird about the size of a chicken.

q: What is the largest island in the world?
f: About 80 percent of Greenland is covered by ice.

q: Which element are both diamonds and graphite made of?
f: Pencil lead is actually graphite.

q: In which country did the ancient Olympic Games begin?
f: The ancient Games began in Olympia in 776 BC.

q: What is the capital of Kazakhstan?
f: Astana has been the capital since 1997.

q: Which mammal can live the longest?
f: Some bowhead whales are thought to live over 200 years.

q: What is the capital of Bhutan?
f: Thimphu is one of the few capitals with no traffic lights.

q: Which tree species grows the tallest?
f: The tallest known redwood is over 115 metres high.

q: Which gemstone is this?
f: Emerald is a green variety of the mineral beryl.

q: What is the capital of Myanmar?
f: Naypyidaw replaced Yangon as the capital in 2006.

q: Which mammal is covered in scales?
f: When threatened, a pangolin rolls up into a tight ball.

q: Which city was Japan's capital for over 1,000 years?
f: Kyoto was the imperial capital from 794 to 1869.

q: What is the largest lizard in the world?
f: Komodo dragons can grow up to 3 metres long.

q: Which country produces the most coffee?
f: Brazil has been the top coffee producer for over 150 years.
